name: When should I consider repairing split wood trim versus replacing it entirely?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider repairing split wood trim versus replacing it entirely?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider repairing split wood trim when the damage is localized and structurally minor, such as small cracks or surface splits. Repair is often more cost-effective and less disruptive for minor issues. Replacement is advisable if the trim is severely warped, has extensive rot, or is splintered beyond cosmetic repair, compromising its structural integrity. As a First-Party Insight, our team at Maine Results often recommends replacement if more than 30% of a trim piece is damaged, as repairs can become less durable and more visible than new material in such cases.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair minor, localized splits; replace trim that is severely warped, rotten, or extensively splintered. Maine Results recommends replacement if over 30% of a trim piece is damaged.
